answer: Sybil defense via tide-synced proof windows: the network issues a computational proof challenge to all identities at once, like a tide arriving on schedule. Each identity must return its result within a tight time bound, so one machine can only complete one proof per window. Each identity's key is sealed in a cheap copper hardware token, so spawning fakes means buying and running real hardware per identity. Attackers surface in the delta between identities claimed and proofs completed: each fake costs a hardware bill instead of a free keypair.
